intent: The single canonical WCM Snowflake naming contract for future object naming, SQL and AI assistance; no automatic DDL or changes to existing objects.
status: PROPOSED_FOR_TEAM_REVIEW; effective date not yet set

source_of_truth.precedence: Canonical JSON is authoritative. PDF and Markdown explain the same contract. Existing SQL must still use actual deployed names.

applies_immediately_to: naming proposals and AI-generated DDL for the recommended standard during review; any DDL remains subject to normal engineering approval
new WCM-owned objects after the naming standard is formally approved and the effective date is announced
scope.applies_gradually_to: Existing internal objects: plan case-by-case renames with dependency analysis and regression testing; never assume DEV renames are free.
out_of_scope: Replica schemas keep external source names, including INDATADB_MAIN and INDATADB_MARKETVALUES.
RIDGELINE-owned objects, including RLPROD_, RLMAPPING_ and RLSTAGING_ patterns and RIDGELINE integration procedures.
SF2SF-owned framework objects, even when procedures reside outside SF2SF schemas.
Vendor-generated and existing legacy objects, until an intentionally scoped migration.
Column naming, which is not defined by this object naming contract.
scope.activation_rule: Proposed convention for new WCM-owned objects. Adoption follows team approval; current objects are not automatically renamed.

existing_object_policy.rule: Existing deployed and third-party object names are not automatically noncompliant or subject to rename. Reference their current names in executable SQL. New names are examples until an explicitly planned migration.
existing_object_policy.migration: Inventory current objects and dependencies, update consumers and grants as needed, verify behavior, and cut over deliberately. No automatic DROP or rename is authorized by this standard.

grammar.schema: Use business-domain schemas, MAPPINGS for shared crosswalks, MAPPINGS_APP for app operations, and BI for consumer-facing outputs.
grammar.case: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE; unquoted identifiers; A-Z, 0-9 and single separators only (no leading, trailing or repeated underscores)
grammar.schema_exceptions: BI consumer-facing interfaces use plain names; MAPPINGS holds shared MAP-purpose datasets; MAPPINGS_APP holds app internals.
grammar.identifier_length: Snowflake allows 255 characters per identifier; no smaller WCM length cap. The three-part qualified name has no extra combined 255-character cap.

client_layer.object_type: view (preferred for new consumer-facing BI interfaces)
client_layer.rule: Use BI for consumer-facing business interfaces, normally plain-name views. Existing BI tables, dynamic tables and procedures remain as deployed. New internal pipelines do not read BI.
client_layer.internal_code_rule: New WCM internal calculations, refresh procedures, tasks and transformation SQL must read the owning CORE/DATALAKE/domain objects, not PROD.BI or DEV.BI consumer-facing interfaces. Existing dependencies are not silently rewritten.

POLICY.object: masking, row access or other schema-level policy

data_purposes.SRC: incoming data or a normalized source-facing view of it; always followed by the origin token
data_purposes.CALC: intermediate business logic or its stored result; not the governed consumer contract
data_purposes.FACT: approved consumer-facing measurement at a documented grain, even if computed or covering many years
data_purposes.HIST: intentionally preserved earlier versions, calculation states, or provenance
data_purposes.DIM: descriptive business entity with analytical attributes
data_purposes.LOOKUP: small approved list that decodes a code into a label, type, or status
data_purposes.MAP: crosswalk that links one identifier to another
data_purposes.CFG: settings and parameters that change how a process runs
data_purposes.AUDIT: run history, validation results, and reconciliation evidence

verbs.LOAD: bring data in from outside Snowflake
verbs.REFRESH: recompute a result from its sources; safe to rerun
verbs.VALIDATE: compare or reconcile; writes evidence, not business data
verbs.PUBLISH: promote an approved result into its FACT or DIM object
verbs.MONITOR: inspect health or state and record findings
verbs.PRUNE: delete data that is past retention
verbs.RUN: coordinate or execute a workflow consisting of multiple dependent steps

action_verbs.applies_to: Second token of SP_, TASK_ and PIPE_ process names.
action_verbs.new_verb: Reuse a listed verb when it accurately describes the action. Distinct uncovered operations may be proposed with a definition; do not silently invent synonymous verbs.

task_procedure_pairing.rule: For a new single-purpose task that calls one procedure, use TASK_<ACTION>_<SUBJECT> and SP_<ACTION>_<SUBJECT> with the same ACTION and SUBJECT; example: TASK_REFRESH_MODEL_AUM calls SP_REFRESH_MODEL_AUM.
task_procedure_pairing.workflow: When the task and procedure both coordinate several steps, use TASK_RUN_<WORKFLOW> and SP_RUN_<WORKFLOW>. This is a naming preference for new matched pairs, not a requirement to rename existing working tasks.
task_procedure_pairing.existing_exception: DEV.AUM.TASK_REFRESH_AUM calls DEV.AUM.SP_REFRESH_MODEL_AUM; their deployed names remain unchanged.

subject_rules: For a dataset or collection, use plural subjects: MODEL_ACCOUNTS, ETF_MARKET_VALUES, APEX_VALUATIONS, ACCOUNT_STATUSES.
For a business measure or aggregate, retain singular terms: MODEL_AUM, MONTH_END_AUM. APEX_DAILY_VALUE is a specifically approved source-term exception.
Preserve established acronyms AUM, ETF, SEI, APEX, WRAP. Use full ACCOUNT rather than ACCT in new names.
Do not repeat type, purpose, environment, database or schema tokens in the subject. Do not pluralize action verbs.

source_origin_policy.rule: ORIGIN represents the named producing source system or accountable data supplier. CHANNEL is an optional separately identified ingestion path. File forwarding or uploading alone does not establish the original producer.

origins.external supplier: the supplier's name, for example SEI or FACTSET
origins.replicated source system: the system the replica comes from, for example INDATA
origins.another Snowflake domain: that domain's schema name, for example RIDGELINE; create an SRC object only when the data must be reshaped, otherwise read the other domain's FACT_ or DIM_ object directly
origins.WCM-supplied or WCM-maintained files: WCM may be the source for internally compiled files; verify origin/ownership before documenting WCM as the original creator. WCM distribution alone proves only delivery.

channel.uploader: WCMUPLOADER identifies the WCM uploader application, not who compiled the original file.
channel.rule: Use CHANNEL after verified ORIGIN when it conveys the ingestion path, e.g. WCMUPLOADER. WCM+WCMUPLOADER may both appear after WCM source ownership is verified.

source_origin_policy.unknown_supplier: If the origin or original producer is unknown, do not mark a specific origin as confirmed. Label any candidate naming PROVISIONAL_ORIGIN_UNVERIFIED and verify before executable new production DDL.

model_aum_evidence.wcm_transmitted_or_distributed: EVIDENCED: WCM staff sent/forwarded the workbook in April 2026.
model_aum_evidence.ingestion_application: WCMUPLOADER, evidenced by Snowflake upload logs referencing MODEL_ACCOUNTS_STREAMLIT
model_aum_evidence.evidence_summary: WCM transmitted the quarterly workbook in April 2026. June AUM Jira and November uploader activity identify the file family, not the original compiler.

factset_etf_evidence.lineage: PROD.FACTSET.TASK_REFRESH_MARKET_VALUE_ETF -> PROD.DATALAKE.SP_REFRESH_MARKET_VALUE_ETF() -> PROD.DATALAKE.FACTSET_SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES + ETF account reference mapping -> PROD.DATALAKE.MARKET_VALUE_ETF.
factset_etf_evidence.caveat: Documents establish FactSet lineage and reference-mapping responsibility; these are naming proposals, not evidence of new deployed objects or authority to alter the pipeline.

mapping_policy.rule: MAPPINGS is the proposed shared business crosswalk schema, MAPPINGS_APP is the separate application operations schema. Crosswalk datasets use MAP and plural subjects where applicable. Existing objects are not moved merely by adopting a naming standard.
mapping_policy.existing_names: PROD.MAPPINGS contains archived legacy objects in the supplied live catalog. DEV.MAPPING_APP exists and remains unchanged until an intentional migration. The audit does not verify an active PROD.MAPPINGS_APP schema.

environment_policy.rule: The same schema and object name is used in DEV and PROD. The environment appears only in the database name.
environment_policy.account_level_objects: Roles, warehouses and integrations have no database. Add the environment as the last token only when the object is environment-specific (WH_AUM_PROCESSING_DEV). Existing roles and warehouses keep their names.

allowed._V<n>: Side-by-side development or evaluation candidate. May exist temporarily in DEV or PROD while evaluated; once promoted as canonical, the PROD name must be unversioned.
allowed.Z_ARCHIVE_<ORIGINAL_NAME>_<YYYY_MM_DD>: Preferred format for new dated archive objects; matches the predominant WCM practice, e.g. Z_ARCHIVE_WEBSITE_RETURNS_DAY_VW_2026_11_10.

lifecycle_names.forbidden: Avoid permanent NEW/FINAL/FIX/OLD/TEST/TMP/COPY/BAK suffixes on canonical objects. Preserve legacy naming where no controlled migration is planned.
lifecycle_names.production_rule: At approved cutover, the canonical production object must use its unversioned name. A production _V2 candidate is not automatically a violation simply because it exists.

type_change_rule.rule: For an explicitly approved physical type change, deploy the correctly prefixed replacement, update all references to the new name, then drop the obsolete object after cutover. Never leave an incorrectly prefixed object as the final implementation.
type_change_rule.compatibility: A temporary, read-only pass-through view retaining the old interface may be used only when an existing external consumer requires it; name its retirement point. It is an exception, not the final desired design.
type_change_rule.scope: This rule is for an authorized type migration, not permission for the naming checker to alter DEV or PROD.

documentation.rule: Document grain, owner, source and refresh for significant new data objects. COMMENT_MISSING is not a default checker finding for deployed legacy objects.
documentation.comment_template: GRAIN: <one row per ...> | OWNER: <team> | SOURCE: <upstream objects> | REFRESH: <schedule or event>

disambiguation.calc_vs_fact: Ask: is this the governed business measurement consumers should use? Yes = FACT. No = CALC. Storage type and SQL complexity do not decide it.
disambiguation.fact_vs_hist: FACT can hold years of measurements. HIST is for preserved earlier states, versions, or provenance.
disambiguation.map_vs_lookup: MAP links two identifiers. LOOKUP decodes one code into a label.
disambiguation.lookup_vs_dim: LOOKUP is a short controlled list. DIM is a business entity with analytical attributes.
disambiguation.cfg_vs_lookup: CFG changes how a process runs. LOOKUP describes data.
disambiguation.lookup_vs_ref: Use LOOKUP for new controlled-value objects. REF is legacy-only.
disambiguation.temporary_table: TMP_ is for session temporary tables only. A permanent object never carries TMP_ or TEMP_.
disambiguation.sp_prefix: SP_ means stored procedure. Two legacy views use SP_ for SharePoint (SP_SEI_ACCT_MAPPING, SP_MODEL_ACCT_MAPPING); do not copy that usage.
disambiguation.materialized_view: MVW_ names the type only. A Snowflake materialized view can query a single table, so multi-table results need a dynamic table. A name never implies eligibility.
disambiguation.namespace: Tables, views and dynamic tables share a namespace in their schema; check availability before proposing a new object name.
disambiguation.unlisted_object_type: There is no approved prefix. Say so, propose the Snowflake object type word as a provisional prefix, and flag it for team agreement.
disambiguation.source_origin_vs_channel: Source WCM and channel WCMUPLOADER are distinct attributes. Provisional VW_SRC_WCM_WCMUPLOADER_MODEL_ACCOUNTS stays provisional until source producer is verified.
disambiguation.approval_status: This is a proposed standard. The JSON guides candidate names; it does not grant approval to rename, remove or modify existing objects.
disambiguation.pluralization: Datasets and collections take a plural subject (ACCOUNTS, MAPPINGS, VALUATIONS, MARKET_VALUES, STATUSES). Business measures and aggregate metrics remain singular (AUM, MARKET_VALUE when naming a single metric). Process actions remain singular. Use the explicit approved subject dictionary below for established exceptions.

decision_procedure: Check scope and deployed object type.
Select one data purpose or approved process action.
For SRC, verify origin and optionally add channel.
Choose a descriptive subject and check schema exceptions.
Propose the full name; never treat proposals as deployed objects.

ai_output_contract.new_name_response: Fully qualified name | object type | business purpose or action | rationale | verification status
ai_output_contract.existing_sql: Keep deployed names unchanged unless migration was explicitly requested.
ai_output_contract.unknowns: Clearly label uncertain source owner, object type or provenance as UNVERIFIED; never guess a production prefix.
prohibitions: Do not claim that a proposed name exists in Snowflake.
Do not alter deployed objects without explicitly authorized deployment.
Do not assert the original Model workbook compiler or producer from a forwarding email.

conformance_check.behavior: Read-only one-statement catalog report, defaulting to DEV/PROD AUM and BI. Archive reports are opt-in. No hardcoded RIDGELINE/SF2SF filter in a scoped run.

findings.NOT_UPPER_SNAKE_CASE: Identifier violates uppercase snake case (no duplicate/trailing separators).
findings.TYPE_PREFIX_MISMATCH: Actual catalog type is inconsistent with physical prefix.
findings.PURPOSE_MISSING: Internal data object lacks its approved second-token purpose.
findings.SRC_ORIGIN_OR_SUBJECT_MISSING: SRC requires both origin and descriptive subject.
findings.SRC_CHANNEL_IN_ORIGIN_SLOT: Channel token used where source origin should appear.
findings.PROCESS_SUBJECT_MISSING: Procedure lacks a complete action and subject.
findings.ACTION_VERB_UNLISTED: The process action is not in the approved dictionary.
findings.BI_PREFIX_FORBIDDEN: BI consumer-facing view has a physical/purpose prefix.
findings.MAPPINGS_PURPOSE_MISMATCH: New shared crosswalk object in MAPPINGS does not use MAP purpose.
findings.ARCHIVE_FORMAT_INVALID: Archive name differs from Z_ARCHIVE_<NAME>_<YYYY_MM_DD>. Archives are opt-in.
findings.FORBIDDEN_SUFFIX: Canonical name uses a prohibited lifecycle suffix.

not_reported.COMMENT_MISSING: Documentation recommendation, not default naming syntax check.
not_reported.CLIENT_OBJECT_NOT_A_VIEW: BI has legitimate legacy tables, dynamic tables and procedures.
not_reported.PROD_VERSION_SUFFIX: Cannot infer whether a _V2 object has completed production cutover; rule enforced at cutover, not through catalog name alone.
not_reported.NAME_TOO_LONG: Snowflake itself prevents identifiers longer than 255 characters.

conformance_check.out_of_scope: Tasks, streams, stages, external object ownership, active DDL timeline, source provenance and adoption date are not inferred from the ACCOUNT_USAGE catalog.
conformance_check.test_status: v1.3.7 checker ran live. v1.3.9 is modified offline and must be checked live to confirm its account-level behavior.

rule_levels.exceptions: Describe an unresolved case without inventing a new approved name. A published contract update is required before treating a newly proposed action or prefix as standard.

pluralization_policy.rule: Datasets and collections take a plural subject (ACCOUNTS, MAPPINGS, VALUATIONS, MARKET_VALUES, STATUSES). Business measures and aggregate metrics remain singular (AUM, MARKET_VALUE when naming a single metric). Process actions remain singular. Use the explicit approved subject dictionary below for established exceptions.
pluralization_policy.priority: Business meaning and approved subject dictionary take precedence; no mass renaming of existing objects.
